`internal/cmd/review.go`: `lode review import --review <id> [--anchors
<sidecar>] < payload.json`. Decode stdin with `critjson.Finish`, save it
beside the sidecar as `finish.json` (or in `os.TempDir()` without one);
build a `model.ReviewRoundInput` per Decisions: `Verdict` from `approved`,
`Client = crit`, `Focused` from `LODE_REVIEW_FOCUSED`, `Threads` from the
unresolved comments in `comments_json`, document mode through the sidecar
(span to byte range, heading trim, section split, crit's `quote` as
`Quote`), change mode through part 2's `(repo, path, side, line,
anchor_text)` anchor from the comment's file and `start_line`; fetch the
review's existing threads and drop every comment whose anchor already has
one; `POST .../rounds`; print what landed: the round number, threads
opened, threads matched to existing ones, spans trimmed or split. The
mapping `critjson.Finish → model.ReviewRoundInput` is a pure function in
`internal/review/critjson/ingest.go` so it is table-tested without a
server. The `--review <id>` flag is not in the WL-REQ-1775 catalogue
entry (`lode review import < result.json`) and needs an amendment to it,
filed with this plan's review.

Server side (WL-REQ-1885): read the TypeSafe docs for the Choice primitive
(https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md) and the API page first.
`internal/review/intent.go` builds the Jev questions (state: the comment's
body, quote and replies, and the subject's kind and title; criteria: the
three WL-REQ-1318 intents with what each means and obliges) and calls the
existing `internal/typesafe` client, the way `internal/inlineref/jev.go`
does. The round handler in `internal/api` classifies a `client = crit`
round's intent-less threads before the store write, never inside it, and
sets `intent_classifier` (`jev` or `default`) and `intent_confidence`.
`worklode_review_intent_classifications_total{outcome, intent}` (outcome
`jev`, `default_unconfigured`, `default_error`) in the review metrics,
registered from `serve.go` (WL-REQ-32).

First tests:

```go
func TestIngestMapsFixture(t *testing.T) {
    in, report := critjson.ToRound(fixture("finish_unresolved.json"), critjson.Options{
        Anchors: sidecarFixture(), Focused: false, Existing: nil})
    // want: Verdict changes_requested, Client crit; one thread per unresolved comment;
    // a comment spanning lines 412..414 → Anchor{Doc: <sidecar doc>, Version: <sidecar version>,
    //   ByteStart: offset of line 412, ByteEnd: end of line 414, Quote: the comment's quote};
    // a comment whose span starts on a heading line is trimmed below it;
    // a comment crossing sec-2 into sec-3 becomes two threads, report names it;
    // every thread's Intent is empty (the server classifies it); resolved comments are skipped.
    // finish_approved.json → Verdict approved, no threads.
}
```

A handler test with a stubbed TypeSafe server: a crit round's threads take
the stubbed choices with `jev` recorded; a `client = cli` thread keeps its
stated intent; an unset key and a 500 from the stub both give
`change_request` with `default`, and the round still lands.

Then the "both reviewer paths" test in `internal/cmd`, with the TypeSafe
stub answering the intents the API-driven review stated: drive one document
review over the API (part 1's test story) to one `changes_requested` round
with a `change_request` and a `question` thread, and a second identical
review by piping `finish_unresolved.json` (its comments placed on the same
spans of the same spec) through `lode review import`; compare the two
reviews' rows with `client`, `intent_classifier`, `intent_confidence`, ids
and timestamps normalized: threads, anchors (rule, version, byte range,
quote), intents, messages, verdicts, state must be equal (WL-REQ-1776).
